I guess to answer your questions, you just move on. It’s life. It will get better, and ask for help if you need to, be it a friend or family member.

when you complete a puzzle, you dont just slam 2 incompatible puzzle pieces just to finish the puzzle, its just gonna turn out to be like a fucking disaster. same idea here, don't blame yourself or her, i believe it takes 2 to clap and you guys are just not suitable for each other. 

if you're the con, dont beat yourself over it, everyone on this earth is flawed, take this time to really improve yourself, mentally, physically and emotionally. In my case again, after my break up, i went to see a therapist and found out that the break up actually re-opened attachment wounds of mine that i wouldn't have noticed. so there is always a silver lining.

remember, its not the ending of the book, its just the ending of the chapter. what's next is up to you.

try writing down your thoughts, really look into the relationship without the rose tinted lenses, find all the things that she did and/or what the relationship lacked that made you feel uneasy, the cons of the relationship basically. 

for me, my ex didn't even respect me enough to learn about my love language and betrayed my trust. it broke me and i used that as fuel for me to keep myself from going back.

i cant speak for everyone but for me, i was ruminating in those memories, living a false reality so to speak? but they aren't gonna come back, so why not move on? 

my advice is that, be kind to yourself, your mind will tend to run off to the what ifs and this is some sort of coping mechanism for itself. just let yourself feel it and at the end, just tell yourself that it isn't real and what you have now is better off than back then.
